object_description: low-rise cluster of terraced volumes arranged around a courtyard
design_condition: The interventions largely preserve the existing arrangement, place new volumes around the courtyard, and use an offset to form an entrance space while leaving the hard-court solution unresolved.

positive.statement: The offset creates a beautifully landscaped entrance area to the main building.

position.rationale: The offset cluster visibly leaves an open approach zone between the main footprints.

positive.statement: The single-story terraced-house type is advantageous for this task.

position.rationale: Low terraced linear volumes are clearly visible in plan and remain near the lower elevation band.

positive.statement: Unbundling the classes into their own units and entrances solves important organizational problems.

position.rationale: The western elongated cluster visibly separates into repeated linear units.

positive.statement: The row of class units is harmonious and very functional.

position.rationale: Repeated parallel traces in the western volume clearly support the row placement.

positive.statement: The internal organization solves the teachers' safety aspect.

position.rationale: Safety relationships are interior and unresolved in the sample; the classroom cluster is the useful anchor.

positive.statement: The solution allows units to be combined, decoupled, or connected and promises great flexibility.

position.rationale: The modular repeated footprint supports an approximate flexibility anchor without showing connections directly.

positive.statement: The multi-purpose room is beautifully located facing the courtyard and has an attractive area facing the lake.

position.rationale: The room is not identifiable; the northeastern volume facing the central court provides a plausible anchor.

negative.statement: The extraordinary spiral staircase is clearly a scale error because there are no representative rooms on the upper floor.

position.rationale: The staircase is absent; an upper-level point above the western classroom cluster is constrained.

negative.statement: The office assigned to the multi-purpose room is placed at the wrong end of the building.

position.rationale: The office is not represented, so it is approximated at the far end of the northeastern volume.

negative.statement: The hall roof is irritating in relation to the existing building and reflects another scale error.

position.rationale: The northeastern volume has a visibly distinct roof trace that supports this scale-related anchor.

negative.statement: The teachers' room is not in the immediate vicinity of the classrooms and the distances are too long.

position.rationale: The room is not visible; the classroom row provides the closest constrained organizational location.

negative.statement: The peripheral location of the economic building is not quite optimal and the route concept needs refinement.

position.rationale: The referenced peripheral building is not distinguishable; the southeastern detached footprint is an approximation.

negative.statement: The open-space project is presented very schematically and leaves many topics unaddressed.

position.rationale: Open-space detail is absent, so the central interstitial landscape is used as a broad constrained marker.

negative.statement: The courtyard design does not meet the requirements of the hard-court surface.

position.rationale: The courtyard void is visibly enclosed by the clustered volumes, though its surface treatment is not sampled.
